judgments.reasoning_cat1: The date line is garbled ("the a4. day of February 1995") and the party is defined as "SENET" though the whole document uses "ENET", a mechanical defect in the very definition of a party. The recitals also use loose descriptions like "excess capacity" and "sole wireless cable system" whose boundaries are not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital conditions ENET's bargain on "issuance to the University of a license authorizing the University to relocate the D Group Station", whereas the operative Sections II.D and II.E allow the Agreement to survive or terminate on various application outcomes, a classic recital-versus-operative tension. The Hybrid recital also sits against Section XIII.Q and Section XIII.M's D2 option.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and a fixed end date (August 29, 1998); nothing to construe in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section I.B (renewal to "ten years from the date hereof") and Section III.A's reference to the same ten-year date, but those fit together without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single sentence stacks two conditions precedent, an "earlier of" pair and a trailing "unless ENET provides ... ninety days notice", so it is genuinely unclear whether the notice exception qualifies the whole renewal or only limb (ii), and whether a further renewal follows the first.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the University will file a licence renewal application, while Section VIII.B expressly lets the University elect not to renew its licence on one year's notice, and Section I.C measures the Right of First Refusal from "the expiration of the automatic renewal term" — the interlock is where a fight would start.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive right to match ... during any or all of the period" is opaque, and "bona fide offer to lease excess capacity" is undefined as to which channels and what counts as bona fide; the reference to "Section LB" is a mis-set cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The right runs two years past a renewal term whose end date is itself contingent under Section I.B, and it must be squared with Section VIII.B (surrender or non-renewal of the licence within the same two years) and Section XIII.A (assignment) — the plainest candidate for a construction dispute in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence — "Such notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — cannot be reconciled with the preceding requirement that notice be given "at the commencement of any negotiations", and "the contract" is undefined (this Agreement or the proposed lease).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also collides with Section I.C.3's seven-day notice on receipt of a bona fide offer and with Section I.B's contingent term end, so the timing machinery of the Right of First Refusal does not cohere across I.C.1-3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Acceptable to the University", "material terms and conditions" and matching "on substantially the same material terms" are all elastic, and the anti-frustration sentence turns on the offer's "purpose or ... effect", a vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its thirty-day exercise window has to be harmonised with I.C.2's one-year advance notice sentence and with I.C.1's two-year window; those timing provisions do not obviously fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any material term ... is subsequently changed" leaves the threshold of materiality open, and "refuses to exercise" does not clearly cover mere silence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates "the procedures specified in the foregoing subsections", which include the internally inconsistent notice timing of I.C.2, so its operation inherits that problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Largely definitional and specific as to the three applications; "as ENET believes necessary" is subjective but is expressly ENET's call.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined terms feed Sections II.B-II.E and III.A consistently; the only friction is Section XII.A's requirement of University approval of all filings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Quality and reliability at least equal", "promptly", and "as the University shall reasonably require" are soft standards, and the refund is "less the University's reasonable costs", an uncapped deduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund of the Commitment Fee here sits against Section II.D.1, where the University "shall retain the commitment fee" on denial, and against Section XIII.N's $15,000 cap on negotiation expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such time as ENET reasonably determines to be provident" is vague and "ECC Applications" is a plain typographical error in a defined term; the $15,000 fee-sharing mechanism is otherwise specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel provision in Section XIII.A says ENET "shall notify" the University about excess fees while this one says ENET "may notify", an inconsistency between two otherwise identical mechanisms; it also cross-refers to "best efforts pursuant to Paragraph XII.A" via Section II.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts", "reasonable requirements of ENET" and "adverse effect" are open-textured, and the proviso that costs be "approved by ENET in advance in writing" reads oddly since ENET is the payer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This paragraph is near-verbatim duplicated at Section III.E.1 (modification of transmission facilities), so a court would have to decide whether the two operate independently or one governs; it is also subordinated by Section XIII.Q to the Hybrid Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls the instrument "this Service Agreement" rather than this Agreement and refers to "the commitment fee" in lower case, mechanical slips; "despite their best efforts pursuant to Paragraph XII.A" is a cross-reference to a later section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retention of the Commitment Fee here squarely opposes Section II.A.2, which requires the University to refund the Commitment Fee if the parties cannot agree on the applications, and the two termination outcomes are not expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts to seek an alternative transmission source" and "cannot be utilized" are judgment-laden but the ten-day mechanism is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Section II.E.2's mirror-image rescission right and with Section III.A's construction obligations; no clear contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Conditions materially adverse to ENET" is the only soft term, and it is coupled with ENET's "sole discretion", which narrows the room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels II.E.2 and II.E.3 and is consistent with Section XI's termination scheme; nothing in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Materially adverse" again, but the notice and rescission periods are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The University's power to rescind ENET's termination is unusual but is expressly stated and mirrored in II.D.2; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause leaves the sequence incomplete — if the University rejects an indemnification offer at its "reasonable discretion", the effect of the earlier termination notice is unstated — and "reasonable discretion" is itself elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to "Paragraph XIIL.A" (a garbled reference to XII.A) and must be read with Section XI.C, which preserves damages claims notwithstanding termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, one-sided allocation of "all reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering" to ENET; "reasonable" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives ENET an uncapped obligation for negotiation and filing costs, whereas Section XIII.N caps legal and engineering fees for negotiating the Agreement at $15,000 and Section II.B caps opposition fees at $15,000 — a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as reasonably possible", "state-of-the-art equipment" and "then-current market value" are all vague, and "until the date that is ten years from the date hereon" is a mechanical error; the equipment-purchase rights turn on distinguishing expiration, nonrenewal and termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to "Section XI.B.(2)" and "Paragraph XI.A" for the $1.00 purchase, so its operation depends on the termination provisions, and the perpetual post-termination use of shared equipment sits awkwardly with Section XI's "without further liability" language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs ENET to reorient antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", but Schedule A is the programming list; that is a mechanical cross-reference error going to the scope of the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section X.B.5 and Schedule B are the actual receive-site schedule, so this provision contradicts the schedule structure of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition trails off — "begun broadcasting the D Group" (station? channels?) — and "the first date of the calendar month after" leaves the triggering event's completion date to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section V.C fixes the first Royalty by reference to the Station being "constructed and ... broadcasting" rather than to the defined Start Date, and Section III.B keys antenna work to the Start Date, so the two triggers may diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Technically qualified personnel", "continuous feed" and the carve-out for "intentional actions or gross negligence of the University" are workable but soft; the parenthetical explanation limits argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENET bears operation and maintenance costs here, while Section XIII.N obliges ENET to reimburse the University for costs the University incurs "operating and maintaining the D Group Station" — overlapping cost allocations that need harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts", "reasonable requirements of ENET" and "adverse effect on the ability of the University to serve its then-existing receive sites" are indeterminate standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section II.C.1 almost word for word and is expressly limited by Section XIII.Q's Hybrid subordination and Section III.E.3's consent requirement, leaving overlap a court might have to sort out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a compound of several vague conditions ("reliable and cost-effective", "no material degradation in quality"), and the reference to digital compression "on channel D1" is unexplained given the capacity split.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IV allocates capacity by reference to D3 and D4 (ENET Capacity) and speaks of digital implementation under III.E.1 or III.E.2 affecting recapture on D3 and D4, so the D1 reference here does not sit comfortably with the capacity scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short prohibition with a familiar "not be unreasonably withheld" qualifier; little to construe beyond reasonableness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restrains the University while Sections II.C.1 and III.E.1 oblige the University to seek modifications at ENET's request, and Section VIII.A obliges the University to preserve the licence; these fit together tolerably.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "SENET Capacity" is a mistyped defined term, and the recapture right to "simultaneous use" of ENET Capacity during stated hours is conceptually obscure alongside the grant of "the entire 6 MHz transmission capacity" to ENET.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recapture right cuts across the exclusive grant in the same sentence and against Section XIII.M (D2 added to ENET Capacity) and Section XIII.P.2 (allocation subject to FCC rule change); the definition of University Capacity as residue drives Section III.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite payment obligation of a stated sum on a stated occasion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fate on early termination is treated inconsistently — refund under Section II.A.2 but retention under Section II.D.1 — though the provision itself takes no position.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is broken — "the greater of: Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) or (ii) Twenty Cents ($0.20) for each subscriber" omits limb (i) — and whether the $0.20 is a monthly per-subscriber figure aggregated is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section V.B.1 supplies the subscriber count method and Section XIII.M sets a parallel D2 royalty in the same "greater of" form, so the structure is at least consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula is garbled — "determined by dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by ENET's then prevailing monthly rate" uses "divided by" twice — and "prevailing monthly rate" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Section V.B's royalty and Section V.C's subscriber certificate without contradicting them; the audit right in V.D is the natural check.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The number of subscribers served during each month of such period" refers to a "period" never identified, and "on twentieth day" drops the article; the trigger is otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The first payment trigger ("constructed and is broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend") is not the defined Start Date in Section III.C, and Section XIII.L expressly excepts royalty payments from the notice rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eighteen-month record-retention period against an audit right exercisable "at any time" during service or within ninety days after, plus "thirty (30) business days' advance written notice", creates a workable but slightly mismatched timetable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only audit mechanism and does not clash with Sections V.B-V.C; the retention period may be shorter than the useful audit window but no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Lawfully modify, waive, rescind, terminate or cancel" is a specific enumeration and the consequence is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the per-subscriber royalty in Section V.B, since ENET's freedom to cancel subscriber contracts affects the royalty base, but the minimum $2,500 floor blunts any real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence proration rule with an obvious method; "proportionately reduced" is self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections V.B and V.C and with the termination provisions of Section XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Royalty ... is the gross charge to ENET" followed by placing all taxes and fees on the University is an unusual and arguably self-contradictory allocation, and "fees" is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against Section XIII.N and Section II.F, under which ENET bears essentially all costs of the arrangement including FCC filing fees under Section VIII.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The measure — cover "of the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations ... of such types and in such amounts as are customarily carried" — is vague, and "including, without limitation" leaves the enumerated minimums as a floor of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The two enumerated policies in VI.A.1-2 and the form requirements in VI.B fit with it; no other provision competes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-risk" at 100% replacement value is a standard and definite specification, though the OCR splits the word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of the enumerated minima under VI.A and is consistent with VI.B's form requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numeric limits per occurrence and in the aggregate; nothing indeterminate beyond the missing final period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VI.A's chapeau and VI.B; no competing liability or indemnity limit exists in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice and the criterion unstated, which is a genuine open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with VI.A and with Section IX.A's indemnity; no direct conflict was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific list of permitted programming closed by "or an other programming agreed to by the University" (a mechanical error for "any other") raises a classic catch-all scope question, and "approval ... which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" sits against the University's "absolute right" to deny obscene programming.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "the programming networks identified on Schedule A hereto", but Schedule A calls itself merely "representative" programming "pursuant to Subparagraph 3 (C)", a section that does not exist, so the permitted-list boundary is unstable; Section IV's grant of use "for any legal purpose ... without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information" also pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts", "all actions reasonably required" and "required or desired" are soft, and the duty not to commit any act "which could reasonably be expected" to imperil the licence is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to "take all necessary steps to renew the licenses" is expressly subject to Section VIII.B, which permits surrender or non-renewal, and it interacts with Section I.B's renewal condition; the exception saves it but the fit is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It grants the University a right to surrender or not renew the licence on one year's notice, but the phrase "at anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term" purports to bind after the Agreement has ended, and "assumeall remaining obligations" is a run-together error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section VIII.A's absolute renewal duty, overlaps almost verbatim with Section XIII.A's assignment machinery, and directly bears on Section I.C's post-term Right of First Refusal and Section I.B's renewal condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limb ends with "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming", a catch-all after a specific list of libel, slander and infringement, and the sub-numbering shifts from (1) to (ii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It indemnifies against programming claims while Section VII gives the University approval rights over programming and Section VI requires liability insurance; those interlock without evident contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional, closed three-limb indemnity mirroring IX.A; the sub-numbering typo does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Symmetrical with IX.A and procedurally governed by IX.C; the asymmetry with ENET's extra programming indemnity is deliberate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" makes the indemnifier's control right hostage to the claimant's satisfaction, an open standard, and "promptly" is unquantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs both IX.A and IX.B uniformly and does not conflict with Section XI.C's preservation of damages claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat representation of Delaware organisation and authority with a forward-looking covenant; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section X.C's survival provision and with the assignment provisions; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall comply with all laws, rules and regulations governing its business and the ITFS facilities" is broad, but as a representation its content is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels X.B.2 and the FCC-related obligations in Sections VIII and XII; no inconsistency detected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short representation about resolutions and authorisations; no term is open to two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section X.B.3 and supports the execution formalities in Section XIII.B; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-litigation representation qualified by "best knowledge"; the qualifier is familiar and the scope is tied to this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels X.B.4, which adds a materiality filter ENET's version lacks, but the asymmetry is not an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a vague and essentially unmeasurable standard, and the party name is mistyped "EENET".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENET's uncapped cost obligations under Sections II.F, III.A, XII.C and XIII.N make the strength of this financial assurance material, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite representation of organisation and eligibility to hold the Licence with a continuing covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The covenant to retain eligibility to hold the Licence sits alongside Section VIII.B's right to surrender the Licence and Section XIII.A's assignment right — a mild tension a court could be asked about.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In all material respects" and "ultra vires" are standard; the representation's content is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It represents no conflict with any other agreement, yet the recitals and Section XIII.Q disclose the pre-existing Hybrid Agreement whose obligations override this one — an arguable inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence of boilerplate corporate authority; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors X.A.3 and supports execution; no conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard litigation representation with a "best knowledge" and adverse-impact qualifier; determinate in application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels X.A.4 and does not clash with any obligation elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about Schedule B; short and definite, though "the lessee of channel D2" is identified only by description.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section III.B directs ENET to reorient antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", which conflicts with this provision's identification of Schedule B as the receive-site schedule; Schedule B itself contains several "Omitted" entries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is a broad and imprecise notification trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes representations continuing, which interacts with the termination-for-material-breach rights in Section XI and the indemnities in Section IX, but without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Material obligations" and "material or substantive measures to cure" are vague, and limb (b)'s parenthetical "(if the breach is other than for the payment of money)" is awkwardly placed so that the relationship between (a) and (b) — alternative or cumulative — is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Termination under this paragraph triggers the $1.00 equipment purchase right in Section III.A and is stated to be "without further liability to ENET", which sits against Section XI.C preserving damages claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) excuses termination "unless such termination is due to a breach by ENET" where the mirror provision assigns fault to the other party, and limb (3) lets ENET walk away simply by ceasing to serve the market — a self-serving, open-ended escape.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section XI.A and Section III.A (which denies the University the $1.00 purchase right where ENET exercises XI.B(2)), limb (3) would let ENET end all obligations at will, in tension with the fixed term in Sections I.A-I.B and the Right of First Refusal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence preserving damages claims for "the terminating party" only — the omission of the terminated party is a notable, arguably deliberate asymmetry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections XI.A and XI.B each say termination is "without further liability", and Sections II.D-II.E repeat that formula, so this provision and those phrases pull in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is syntactically mangled — "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, required to secure FCC approval" — so what the approval qualifier attaches to is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its absolute bar on any FCC filing without the University's prior consent sits against Section II.A.1 and II.C.1, where ENET prepares applications and amendments the University is obliged to file, and against Section III.E.2's application obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision uses "best reasonable efforts" and then "reasonable best efforts" for different duties, and requires the University to file "such reasonable protests or other petitions to deny ... as may be requested by ENET", an open-ended obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to obtain and maintain licences overlaps Section VIII.A, and reimbursement is separately addressed in Sections XII.C and XIII.N; the overlap is redundant rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence repeats "incurred by the University" twice and omits the object of "reimburse all reasonable costs", but its meaning is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of three overlapping expense provisions (II.F, XII.C, XIII.N), one of which caps negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000 while this one is uncapped for Section XII obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — "Subject to the foregoing provisions, the University may assign its authorization to an entity that does not agree to assume all remaining obligations" — contradicts the first sentence's condition that the assignee assume those obligations, an internal self-cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section VIII.B's one-year-notice and designation machinery almost verbatim while producing a different trigger, and it bears directly on Section I.C's Right of First Refusal and Section X.B.1's covenant to remain eligible to hold the Licence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts language; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the execution block and Section XIII.D's writing requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It opens with a statement of intention and then imposes duties to "assist in the development of such program" and make "addressing facilities available" without any standard, scope or cost allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The programme would use University Capacity as defined in Section IV, and the guide listing depends on ENET's production schedule; no direct conflict, but the aspirational framing sits oddly beside the operative "shall".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional merger and written-modification clause; its terms are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement repeatedly incorporates and subordinates itself to the Hybrid Agreement (recitals, Sections II.C.1, III.E.1, XIII.Q), which sits uneasily with a clause superseding all pre-existing agreements "with respect thereto".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of executory character with no operative content; its legal effect is unclear but there is little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the continuing obligations in Sections III and VIII and would matter in insolvency, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of excusing events closes with "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties", a catch-all after specifics that invites an ejusdem generis argument, and "period of dependency" appears to be an error for pendency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parenthetical "(nor shall any charges or payments be made in respect thereof)" would suspend the minimum monthly Royalty under Section V.B, and it overrides Section XIII.R's time-of-the-essence clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts" and a broad negative covenant not to "adversely affect the rights granted", but the language is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The negative covenant is arguably inconsistent with the University's express rights to surrender the licence (VIII.B), assign (XIII.A) and recapture capacity (IV) — a court could be asked to reconcile them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Choosing federal communications law, FCC Rules and District of Columbia law together is unusual, but each source is identified precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section XIII.J (no contra proferentem) and Section XIII.K (DC courts); no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings clause; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several substantive cross-references in the document are made by section heading and number, but the clause only demotes headings, which is conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disclaims contra proferentem in clear terms; the only softness is what counts as a rule of construction "under which a document is to be construed more strictly against the drafting party".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It would be invoked precisely because other provisions (the Right of First Refusal, the assignment clause) are ambiguous, but it does not contradict any of them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any party shall have the right to sue the other party in District of Columbia courts" is permissive in form yet paired with an irrevocable submission and waiver of all venue objections, leaving exclusivity genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "the section concerning Notices herein" (XIII.L) for service and coexists with Section XIII.H's governing law; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" is a loose cross-reference, and the deemed-receipt rule (first weekday after sending) is otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section V.C requires Royalty payments by first class mail, which this exception preserves, and Section XIII.K relies on this section for service; the fit is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls the entitlement both an "exclusive tight to lease" and an "option", ties the exercise window to a notice the University may never give, and "for the duration of this Agreement" is ambiguous as to renewal terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An exclusive right over channel D2 collides with Section XIII.Q, which subordinates everything to the Hybrid Agreement covering D2, and with Section IV's definition of ENET Capacity as D3 and D4; the extra royalty formula also echoes Section V.B's broken "greater of" structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" opens an obligation to reimburse "all reasonable costs and expenses" with a $15,000 cap that grammatically attaches only to negotiation fees, leaving the rest uncapped and the cap's reach contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps and arguably conflicts with Section II.F (uncapped negotiation costs to ENET), Section XII.C, and Section III.D (ENET bears operation and maintenance costs at its own expense while here it reimburses the University for the same).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short no-joint-venture clause; "airtime use relationship" is undefined but the negative is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parties' extensive cooperation duties (Sections VIII, XII) do not contradict a disclaimer of joint venture status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Negotiate in good faith to reform and amend" is an agreement to agree with no fallback, and "contributes to such adverse amendment" is a vague prohibition on regulatory advocacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside Section XIII.P.2's acknowledgement that FCC rules may change the capacity allocation and Section XIII.D's written-modification requirement; the fit is loose but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of regulatory risk with a mis-cited release date (July 9 versus July 6 in Section IV); little operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It concedes that the capacity allocation is subject to future FCC rule changes, which cuts against Section IV's fixed allocation of D3/D4 and Section XIII.P.1's reformation duty — an acknowledgement pointing away from the operative grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be read to conform to such other obligations that the University may owe to Hybrid" makes ENET's rights subject to an external contract of unstated content, and "reasonable judgment of the University after consultation with Hybrid" gives one party the decisive say.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" override directly limits Section XIII.M's exclusive D2 option and Section IV's capacity grant, and it is the mechanism by which any conflict between this Agreement and the Hybrid Agreement is resolved against ENET.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence making every stated time of the essence; blunt but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with Section XIII.F, which automatically extends time for performance on force majeure, and with the many "promptly"/"as soon as reasonably possible" duties that fix no time at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is clumsily worded — a waiver shall not waive "any other failure in the future or in the past" — which leaves the effect of a past waiver on the same obligation uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on the cure and termination mechanics in Section XI and the notice requirements throughout, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions of "including" and "Final Order" are precise and conventional; "any variations therefore" is a typo for "therefor" that changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Final Order" is used throughout Sections II.D, II.E, III.A, VIII.B and XIII.A consistently with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It describes the list as "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit", which is a statement of intention rather than a defined permitted list, and it cites "Subparagraph 3 (C)", a provision that does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as identifying "the programming networks" ENET may transmit without further approval, so the Schedule's merely "representative" character and its dangling cross-reference cannot be squared with the operative programming clause; Section III.B also mis-cites Schedule A for receive sites.
